subject: [enc4k] H.264 'quality collapse' was a MEASUREMENT BUG in vcodec_check.py stats (BT.709 VUI -> ffmpeg colour conversion); real H.264 PSNR 51-61 dB; fixed
body: The vendor H.264 encoder writes VUI colour_primaries/matrix = 1 (BT.709) for widths >= 1280 and 5 (BT.601) below (and for HEVC). My stats filtergraph compared the bt709-tagged decode with the untagged raw reference via format=yuv420p, and ffmpeg's format negotiation inserted a BT.709->BT.601 conversion: ~27 dB for every wide H.264 stream, independent of profile/level/size (that is why it was constant 27.2-27.4). Pixelwise check of vc21 1280x720 frame 0: per-MB MSE < 1 everywhere; raw-vs-raw psnr of vc21 1080p: Y 51.45 dB. Fixed (decoded stream setparams colorspace/primaries/trc=unknown, range=tv). Re-run on vc21: 1920x1080 Baseline 51.6 avg (min 47.8), Main 51.6, HIGH 60.9 avg (min 48.2), 1920x480 51.4, 1280x720 51.2, 640x1080 51.3, 640x480 51.1, 4K H.264 (vc18) 46.1 avg (min 43.0) at 33 Mbit/s, HEVC 1080p 55.6. So there is NO H.264 parameter problem; High profile works in hardware and is the best preset. Re-check older fetches with: python3 gpu/build/apps-20261104/vcodec_check.py stats <stream> --log <probe.log>. Next from me: restart-on-switch (vcodecd + probe retry, IP 1091/1091) payload, then the kern.n2vc.venc_fast proposal.
